internal.title: Incident Resolved: Checkout Service Error Rate Spike Due to Payment Service Failure
internal.body:
At 11:35 UTC on 2026-11-08, an alert was triggered for a high error rate in the checkout service. Investigation identified the root cause as an error injection in the payment service, specifically related to invalid card token errors causing failed charges. This was confirmed by logs and trace evidence. The paymentFailure flag was disabled at 11:55 UTC, leading to rapid recovery of the service error rate to normal levels. The incident was resolved promptly with no further impact.

Timeline:
- 11:35:51: Alert received for high error rate in checkout
- 11:55:38: Diagnosis confirmed payment service error injection
- 11:55:40: Disabled paymentFailure flag after approval
- 11:55:40: Verified recovery of error rate

Actions taken:
- Disabled paymentFailure flag to stop error injection

Please review the postmortem for detailed analysis and lessons learned.

external.title: Some checkouts failed due to payment processing issues
external.body: Between 11:35 and 11:55 UTC on 2026-11-08, some customers experienced issues completing checkout due to a problem in the payment processing system. The issue was identified and resolved promptly, and normal service has been restored. We apologize for any inconvenience caused and appreciate your understanding.

output.summary: A spike in checkout service errors was caused by a payment service failure involving invalid card token errors. Disabling the related error injection flag resolved the issue.
output.impact: Customers experienced failed checkout attempts due to payment processing errors between 11:35 and 11:55 UTC.
output.root_cause: An error injection in the payment service caused invalid card token errors, leading to failed charges and increased checkout errors.
output.resolution: The paymentFailure error injection flag was disabled after diagnosis and approval, resulting in recovery of the checkout service error rate.

lessons.lesson: Ensure rapid diagnosis and flag toggling procedures are in place for error injections to minimize customer impact.
lessons.applies_when: When an error injection flag is causing service errors and can be toggled to mitigate impact.

action_items: Review and improve monitoring for payment service error injections.
Enhance alerting to include direct linkage between payment errors and checkout failures.
Conduct a drill to practice rapid flag toggling and recovery verification.
